concept_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the supplied side-by-side Holy Diver gameplay comparison screenshot. Change ONLY the foreground gold collision masonry and tall foreground masonry supports in the RIGHT HALF. Keep the LEFT HALF exactly unchanged as the original-game reference. Keep the beautiful navy-and-gold palace BACKGROUND in the right half exactly unchanged, including its distant arches, decorative background columns, banners and windows; also preserve the player, enemies, spells, HUD and gameplay layout. Replace the flat, repetitive sharp square slabs in the right foreground with attractive hand-carved golden sandstone: irregularly worn and slightly rounded bevels, broad horizontal stone courses, warm top lips, deep ochre side shadows and rich material depth, consistent with polished SNES/GBA fantasy platformer art. The tall narrow foreground block-stack pillars (one rising through the floor near the center of the right half, another descending from the ceiling) should instead look like coherent ornate carved gold temple columns with shaped capitals, continuous fluted shafts and molded bases, all fitting the SAME silhouettes and collision footprint. Do not add bulky overhangs or move any platform edge. This is a visual design study for the material revision, not a new level layout. Avoid uniform tiled wallpaper, plain rectangular cubes, plastic, smooth 3D rendering, new text or changes to the approved backdrop.
asset_prompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: transparent reusable game terrain sprite derived from the selected Holy Diver screenshot (image 1); image 2 is the new stonework design direction. Extract and redesign ONE nonbreakable gold sandstone platform block as an isolated horizontal block, exactly front-on, approximately 2:1 width to height. Worn rounded and lightly chipped corners, thick raised warm top rim, subtle scalloped perimeter, broad ochre stone face, carved bevel, rich dark amber lower and side shading. Solid and sturdy with small surface wear but NO deep fractures. Similar to the softened horizontal blocks in image 2, rather than the flat sharp square slabs in image 1. High-quality hand-painted SNES/GBA fantasy game sprite, readable when reduced to 64x32 pixels. The opaque face should occupy nearly the entire rectangular footprint, with only 1-2 pixels worth of corner rounding at final scale. No text, no symbols, no floor, no shadow outside the block, no perspective side extrusion, no surrounding scene. Actual transparent background.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one transparent breakable-block game sprite derived from the supplied Holy Diver screenshot (image 1); image 2 is the stonework style direction. Make one distinct destructible temple block, exactly front-on and square footprint, for a 32x32-pixel final sprite. Warm bronze/gold carved beveled frame with slightly rounded chipped corners around a darker recessed desaturated bronze sandstone face. Show ONE clear branching jagged crack across the recessed face, with a few chipped fragments still attached, so it reads immediately as breakable and fragile at small size. The darker inset and fracture must distinguish it from the solid warm sandstone blocks; do not just add hairline noise. Rich hand-painted SNES/GBA Gothic fantasy sprite matching the temple. Keep nearly the full square collision footprint; no large transparent holes. No letters, no runes, no icon, no scene, no detached particles, no drop shadow. Actual transparent background.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one transparent modular indoor temple pillar sprite derived from the selected Holy Diver screenshot (image 1); image 2 shows the desired replacement of the plain foreground block stacks. Isolate and refine that coherent carved GOLD STONE COLUMN into a complete single front-view vertical pillar: broad carved acanthus capital at top, narrow molded neck, continuous long rounded fluted shaft with deep dark bronze grooves and warm ivory-gold front light, then molded stone plinth at bottom. Overall width to height about 1:4. Important for game geometry: the capital, shaft and base all stay within the same straight outer width; the shaft should be substantial, almost full width, with curved shaded side surfaces rather than widely overhanging caps. Shaft fills the middle two thirds and has NO horizontal brick seams. Capital and base are each clearly separated reusable portions; body can repeat vertically. This is a structural foreground pillar, not a decorative backdrop. High-quality hand-painted 16-bit Gothic fantasy game art, crisp enough to reduce to 64 pixels wide. Avoid photorealism, flat square stacks, cropped ends, dramatic perspective, background architecture, text, casts of shadows outside the pillar. Actual transparent background.
